root_cause.instructions: Which root cause best explains the plant facts?

criteria.RCA-09: Deflagration on re-ignition of an accumulated un-burnt fuel-air mixture, made possible by a passing oil-burner shut-off valve and by omission of the mandatory purge. Systemic: a safety-critical interlock (purge permissive) could be defeated by a single operator without authorisation or review, within a management system that tolerated known passing fuel valves and repeated flame failures as routine.
criteria.RCA-10: Loss of a stable light-up flame from degraded atomisation - water and sediment in the LDO choked the burner nozzle, with low atomising steam pressure and marginal combustion air, so the flame could not sustain itself; a separately developing photocell fouling added a false loss-of-flame indication. Systemic: the whole light-up system is standby equipment maintained reactively, so multiple hidden failures accumulated and appeared together on demand.
criteria.RCA-15: Insufficient primary air velocity in one branch line after a PA damper was left throttled following maintenance, so the line dynamic pressure could no longer oppose the fluidised-bed static head and hot particles back-flowed and accumulated in the vertical portion. Systemic: no post-maintenance restoration checklist for damper positions, no compartment-wise PA flow measurement, and no PA line temperature monitoring.
criteria.RCA-11: Fireside erosion of a water wall tube by circulating bed material in the high-velocity bed-to-freeboard transition zone, progressively thinning the wall until it split longitudinally; internal deposits contributed by raising local metal temperature. Systemic: a foreseeable wear-out mechanism with no thickness-monitoring task, wear shields removed without engineering review, and an uncontrolled operating envelope (excess air, bed height, ash abrasiveness).
